transcript.answer: No, not any more. Originally (task 044) the client cleared `busy` on `stream_end`, on an `error` frame, or on socket close. Issue #191 and PR #290 (merged 2026-09-29, commit e131e7b) changed that. The error branch now only records the error, so `state.error` is still set. The client clears `busy` only on `stream_end` or on socket close. The reason is that HAL Engine 0.3.0 sends exactly one `stream_end` per accepted message, whether or not it errored. It can also send an unrelated `error`, such as an INVALID_MESSAGE for another malformed frame, in the middle of a healthy stream. Clearing `busy` on that frame would drop the typing indicator and unlock the composer mid-answer.

judgements.reason: The answer says no, explains that an INVALID_MESSAGE error can arrive mid-stream, that stream_end is sent exactly once per accepted message, and that busy clears only on stream_end or socket close, which matches all essentials of the gold answer.
